column1: # Charging headroom of each aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase: capacity (kcat x copies per cell, at saturating substrates) over
# amino acid usage, from Dykeman, E. (2025) PLoS Comput Biol. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1013353 (S1 Text,
# Table I and Tab E), linearly interpolated in growth rate to the basal (0.945 per h) and with_aa (1.66 per h) conditions.
# Dykeman's usage is sized for post-upshift elongation (about 19 aa/s), so these margins are about 1.09x smaller than
# against steady-state demand. The ParCa charging fit (reconstruction/ecoli/fit_trna_charging.py) gives each synthetase
# at least this capacity over the model's own demand.
# The ParCa fit replaces the Ala margin (alaS) with the median of the other synthetases' margins (about 1.38; the
# values below are left as published). Dykeman lowered AlaRS turnover to about 10 /s to respect the single-turnover
# transfer rate (16.4 /s; S1 Text section 3), reports AlaRS as his largest kcat discrepancy (6.6x above in vitro) and
# notes that the AlaRS kcat or proteomics need revisiting (main text). The 1.14 margin therefore reflects constraints in
# his fit rather than a measured limit. With 1.14, with_aa Ala was 56-58% uncharged and drove RelA and ppGpp up.
